top_stories.title: Mid and smallcaps get the money as Nifty lags - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Advance-Decline Ratio (ADR)** for BSE stocks remained strong in May, with the ratio exceeding one for two consecutive months.  **Nifty Midcap 100** and **Nifty Smallcap 100** indices reached record highs in May, while the **Nifty** and **Sensex** benchmarks experienced declines. Analysts predict that midcaps and smallcaps will outperform the Nifty in the coming months, with potential for gains in the midcap index to reach 63,500 levels and the smallcap index to test its record high around 19,600.

top_stories.title: MSCI confirms early index inclusion rules ahead of SpaceX IPO - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: **SpaceX**, led by **Elon Musk**, is expected to join the MSCI indexes, potentially attracting trillions of dollars in assets from passively managed funds. The rocket maker's $75 billion fundraising and $1.75 trillion valuation have met the size and free-float thresholds for early inclusion.  However, S&P Global has excluded **SpaceX** from its S&P 500 index due to its lack of profitability. Trading on Nasdaq is scheduled to begin June 12th, with MSCI's decision expected within ten trading days.

top_stories.title: NLC India shares fall 3% as OFS worth up to Rs 1,263 crore opens - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **government** will sell a 3% stake in **NLC India**, the country's leading mining and power generation company, through an offer for sale (OFS). The OFS opens to non-retail investors on June 9th with retail investors joining on June 10th.  The government aims to raise approximately Rs 1,263.51 crore from the sale of 4.17 crore shares at a floor price of Rs 303 per share. **NLC India** has seen its share price fluctuate in recent months but overall remains up over 31% in 2026.

top_stories.title: Somali referee Omar Abdulkadir Artan denied entry to USA for FIFA World Cup | Football News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Omar Abdulkadir Artan**, a Somali referee selected for the 2026 World Cup, was denied entry to the United States by **US Customs and Border Protection**.  The **FIFA** confirmed that he would be unable to officiate at the tournament.  **A senior adviser to Somalia’s Ministry of Youth and Sports** stated that Artan had valid documents and a diplomatic passport issued to facilitate travel after previous visa-related difficulties, but was still denied entry due to vetting concerns.

top_stories.title: NLC India shares fall 3% as OFS worth up to Rs 1,263 crore opens - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Central government** will sell 3% of its stake in **NLC India**, a leading mining and power generation company, through an offer for sale (OFS) starting on June 9th. The OFS offers around 4.17 crore shares at a floor price of Rs 303 each, raising approximately Rs 1,263.51 crore. **NLC India** has seen its share price fluctuate recently but overall remains up over 31% in 2026. The government is ramping up disinvestment efforts and this sale follows similar offloading of stakes in other public sector undertakings (PSUs).

top_stories.title: Ayali switches to Amritpal’s party, puts panthic unity to another political test | Chandigarh News - The Indian Express
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Manpreet Singh Ayali**, a three-time Dakha MLA, is set to formally join the **Amritpal Singh**-led **Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De)** in Chandigarh on Tuesday.  Ayali's move strengthens the fledgling outfit and marks another chapter in the ongoing realignment of **Punjab’s Akali politics**. The decision comes after Ayali resigned from all posts of the **SAD (Punar Surjit)**, a breakaway faction of the **Shiromani Akali Dal**, and expressed his desire for a unified Panthic platform.  Ayali's departure further reduces the **SAD**’s legislative strength, but senior leaders maintain that the party still has a strong grassroots base.

top_stories.title: "Lovers' Spat": Israeli Envoy On Trump's Iran Ultimatum To Netanyahu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Iran** and **Israel** have halted hostilities following a series of strikes that threatened regional war.  **Donald Trump**, US President, reportedly warned **Benjamin Netanyahu**, the Israeli Prime Minister, against escalating attacks on **Iran**, citing potential loss of US support. **Yechiel Leiter**, Israel's ambassador to the US, denied reports of an ultimatum and characterized US-Israel talks as cooperative. While **Netanyahu** asserted Israel's right to self-defense, Iranian officials vowed a prolonged conflict and threatened further strikes against US interests in the region.

top_stories.title: West Bengal Trinamool Leader Former Bidhannagar Mayor Sabyasachi Dutta Arrested On Extortion Charges
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Sabyasachi Dutta**, former Biddhannagar mayor and a known political turncoat, was arrested on extortion charges.  The businessman who filed the complaint alleged that **Dutta** extorted lakhs of rupees from him in 2018. This arrest comes as investigative agencies tighten their grip on several prominent Trinamool leaders following the party's loss in West Bengal. The developments add to a string of desertions and arrests, including former minister Sujit Bose, and are occurring amidst a massive internal rebellion within the party.

top_stories.title: Explained: Why Bharti Airtel, Vodafone Idea shares rallied up to 4% on Tuesday - The Economic Times
top_stories.rephrased_article: The **Bombay High Court** ruled that the **Indian government** lacked legal authority to impose a one-time spectrum charge on telecom operators, providing relief of around Rs 20,000 crore to **Vodafone Idea** and **Bharti Airtel**. The court struck down demand notices issued by the Centre for recovery of OTSC, ordered the return of bank guarantees, and declared all related orders concerning the charge invalid.  The dispute stems from a 2012 Union Cabinet decision that imposed a one-time charge on spectrum holdings exceeding 6.2 MHz, which was challenged by both companies. The court emphasized that the government's actions exceeded contractual and licensing arrangements with telecom operators.

top_stories.title: Kerala 'Islam-Friendly' Gym Row Deepens Amid Ownership Questions
top_stories.rephrased_article: A controversy has erupted in Kerala's Palakkad over an unfinished gym, ASB Fitness Centre, promoted by **Nawas Muthu** as "Islamic-friendly".  **Ahmed Settu** and **Shahul Hameed**, who claim to be the long-time operators of the facility, deny **Muthu's** ownership and involvement.  The controversy stems from **Muthu's** proposed time slots for women with no music, separate timings for men and women, dress code requirements, and restrictions on "unnecessary conversations" which were criticized as promoting religious segregation. While police sources confirmed the gym was not operational when the controversy erupted, BJP activists have filed a complaint alleging that the facility promotes religious segregation and seeks action under multiple provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
